page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g7se.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance within the Enhanced family, designed around a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8369B processor running at a base clock frequency of 2.9 GHz. The CPU architecture supports x86_64 instructions alongside hardware extensions such as AVX-512, AVX-512 VNNI, AES-NI, and SHA-NI. The instance allocates 16.0 GB of system memory, translating to 4.0 GB per vCPU, with 48 MB of shared L3 cache and 1 MB of L2 cache per core.

The hardware configuration does not bundle local disk storage, requiring external cloud storage volumes for all persistent data operations. Network capabilities include a baseline throughput of 2 Gbps, managed via the KVM hypervisor. No dedicated GPU accelerators are attached to this instance profile.

Benchmark results highlight solid single-thread execution paired with moderate parallel computing metrics. In Geekbench testing, the instance achieved a single-core score of 1556.0, ranking in the middle tier, while its multi-core result of 3338.0 reflects typical scaling limitations of a dual-core, four-thread physical footprint. Memory bandwidth throughput recorded 30.13 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 24.19 GB/sec on writes. Synthetic caching and parsing routines demonstrated capable throughput, yielding 27.8 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 109.67 tokens/sec during 135M model LLM text generation.

Cost efficiency is centered on predictable resource allocation for moderate, continuous system loads. Because the platform delivers dedicated hardware cores without burstable CPU credits, it provides stable performance for balanced microservices, static web serving, caching layers, and lightweight enterprise application hosting.

Accompanied by 16.0 GB of system memory, it maintains a standard 1:4 core-to-memory balance. The instance provides 2 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth, operates without bundled local storage, and includes no GPU hardware. Synthetic performance tests reveal balanced single-thread capability, illustrated by a Geekbench single-core score of 1556.0 and consistent gzip compression rates, balanced against modest multi-core throughput typical of a four-thread footprint. Instruction extensions such as AVX-512 and cryptographic offloading are supported natively. This instance is best suited for general application hosting, lightweight caching with Redis, internal tooling, and standard microservices.
